research.scope: Read-only node/port inventory and numeric mapping verification

images.name: One LFO → three Rosette parameters
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE landscape 3:2 low-fidelity software interaction study on UNIFORM WHITE PAPER with rough DARK GRAY PENCIL outlines. No dark background, glow halo, decorative shading, chrome, glass, hardware, waveform graphs, sidebar or inspector. Flat straight-on wireframe. Amber cables ONLY for numeric signals; gray cable with crosshair glyph for position fields; muted violet for picture/color. Nodes are simple rounded rectangles dominated by simple rough visual previews. Small legible handwritten node names outside nodes allowed because this study tests actual named node types. Show exactly the concrete graph below. An enlarged connector is attached directly to target LEFT edge; it grows from the input sockets as a coherent part of the node, with a single shared outline. Target picture body stays dominant. Small software concentric dials use gray center pointer for base, amber outer arc for signed depth. Never draw a range knob on a position or picture route. Each connection must have an unambiguous source and target. No arbitrary extra nodes. Labels listed below only. Main graph upper two-thirds, one small quiet before/after preview pair bottom right where requested. Keep generous whitespace. This is a proposed bundled routing UI over real node ports, not a production UI.
Show left source node labeled "LFO", containing one amber dot, single output labeled "n". One amber cable leaves n and reaches a compact circular bundle entry on a joined vertical connector at LEFT edge of large right target labeled "Form / Rosette". Target preview is a rough sculptural rosette made of several looping hoops, NOT concentric flat rings. The joined connector contains exactly THREE vertically stacked small concentric controls, labeled "spread", "tumble", "flare". Inside connector, the incoming cable branches visibly to these three controls. Different arc lengths, and flare arc points opposite direction. A tiny "3" on collapsed bundle entry signals three routes. Labels "spread", "tumble", "flare" are real parameter names. Under graph show TWO small previews of the same hoop sculpture, one compact and softly shaded, one opened and tilted with stronger gray intensity. Small text "one rhythm" permitted. No separate LFOs for each parameter, no extra output. Source single n feeds all three inlets. User should read one coherent gesture with three independently adjustable amounts.
images.assessment: One source can coordinate spread, tumble and flare with independent signed depths. Generated study communicates fan-out but drifts into a permanent parameter strip, a waveform and a sculptural product rendering. Those are not selected UI directions.

Two main nodes only. Left labeled "Polar", preview a gray radial coordinate field with a crosshair and thin spokes. It has EXACTLY TWO right output sockets labelled "radius" and "angle". Shade's joined left connector has EXACTLY TWO numeric concentric controls labeled "n" and "amount". TWO parallel amber cables form one closely grouped bundle with a small shared middle sleeve but remain individually traceable: upper radius cable to upper n control; lower angle cable to lower amount control. Never cross cables or merge their values. Each destination has its own amber depth arc. A small expanded view is the main graph itself, not a floating inspector. Bottom labels permitted: "radius → palette position", "angle → brightness / opacity", "spatial fields". No LFO pulse dot, no time symbols; these are spatial numeric fields rather than two oscillators. No additional nodes.
images.assessment: Two outputs remain distinct: radius feeds palette position n; angle feeds amount. Joined controls read coherently. The sleeve needs interaction to make clear it bundles routes rather than combining values. Picture is illustrative, not renderer output.

No claim this mechanism exists today.
images.assessment: Proposed connector-local mixing exposes source weights, combination mode, and target depth. Lens c picture feed is valid. Mixing is not implemented. Attachment is too large and sources wrongly show waveforms; these are generated concept limitations.

Three nodes arranged left to right in one CLEAR directed chain. First small node labeled "LFO A" with amber pulse dot and output "n". Neon preview contains a rough gray outlined star surrounded by a few close gray contour lines suggesting halo, no actual rendered glow. Every knob has base pointer and signed amber amount arc. Above first numeric cable write "changes speed"; above second write "changes halo". Below graph show two small star previews, narrow then wider gray halo contour spacing. No FM label, no mutual arrows or feedback. This is a concrete chain using real existing rate and halo ports; smooth FM behavior is not asserted.
images.assessment: Superseded draft: incorrectly draws a picture input into Neon and invents an img label. Retained for provenance; use corrected image.

images.name: LFO → LFO → Neon — corrected
images.prompt: Edit the attached rough wireframe while preserving its white-paper pencil style and main three-node rate-modulation chain. Make these precise correctness changes: Glow / Neon DOES NOT have a picture input. Replace the upper violet cable and its "image (from elsewhere)" label with an AMBER numeric cable labeled "Figure / Star · d" from off canvas. Change its entry label from "img" to exactly "d". This cable carries the shape distance field from a Star node into Neon d; do not draw an image input. Keep LFO A.n→LFO B.rate→(B.n)→Glow/Neon.halo unchanged. Remove the waveform curves inside BOTH LFO nodes; retain only a single small amber pulse dot inside each. All other node placement and the star preview and narrow/wide halo comparison unchanged. No extra controls, no dark background, no glow halo outside the picture previews.
images.assessment: Corrected numeric Figure/Star.d → Glow/Neon.d feed, with LFO A.n → LFO B.rate and B.n → Neon.halo. Waveforms removed. Actual rate modulation may jump; smooth FM needs engine work. Previews are illustrative.
